scope: Three factions, 25 army-level strategic plans each. Original game design informed by the earlier official StarCraft references, not a claim that all 75 are named StarCraft strategies.
design_level: Primary army composition, support units, macro objective and operating method. Individual abilities are subordinate actions, not additional strategies.
rules: Each higher difficulty adds to the preceding repertoire; it does not discard earlier strategies.
Weighted random selection uses only scouted enemy information and time-limited memory. No hidden enemy-state reads, free resources or stronger unit stats.
Every mission budgets real resources, prerequisites, population, transports and legal unload ground. Transport capacity is passenger population sum 8, not StarCraft slot counts.
Prepare, assemble outside enemy defenses, wait for slow members, enter together, then retreat/regroup on heavy loss. Do not stream single reinforcements to their deaths.
Defend home first; cancel a planned drop if anti-air covers both approach and unloading. Replan after observed enemy composition changes, not every simulation tick.
Scout and target priorities cannot bypass fog, cloak detection, terrain elevation or weapon ground/air restrictions.
None of these advanced missions may be implemented until the user reviews the tactics below.
Final user correction: 25 large army/strategy plans for each faction, 75 total. Earlier 40/60 counts and micro-only additions are superseded.
Production weights and build orders belong to each army plan; no free units, instant tech, forced enemy reactions or stat bonuses.
Pure ground/air-specialized armies must transition or bring support when scouting reveals counters. Nova fighters and Araowl moon fighters cannot attack ground.
Skills including smoke, bind, cleanse, scatter and repair belong inside these army plans; do not count them as separate large strategies.
